newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says seeks numerical targets for deficit cuts.
newsitem.headline: MOF says seeks numerical targets for deficit cuts.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday that he hoped that numerical targets for deficit reduction would become law.
"In order to realise various reforms and to realise numerical targets (for deficit reduction) I hope we will be able to legalise detailed steps for achieving those goals," he said.
Asked whether the government would submit deficit reduction bills to the next session of parliament, he said this was unlikely.

Mitsuzuka said he hoped to settle a bilateral dispute with the United States over insurance by December 14, a day before mutually agreed deadline. Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky is due to arrive in Tokyo on Saturday for the ministerial talks.
Mitsuzuka said the negotiations would be "tough".
He said it was important for both sides to abide by international rules and to discuss the issue based on free market principles.
